name: KY-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+23 partisan lean in a heavily Republican western Kentucky district
Comer's incumbency and $3.0M cash advantage over Williams' $210K raised
Prediction markets price Comer near 96% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The district's R+23 lean, Comer's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing him around 96% all point to a safe Republican hold, with only a modest Democratic environment offsetting the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected Comer retirement would be the main route to a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
James Comer, the incumbent Republican, is heavily favored in this western Kentucky district, which leans about 23 points Republican at the presidential level. He has raised nearly $1.9 million and holds $3.0 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Drew Williams has raised about $211,000 with no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets give Comer roughly a 96% chance of winning.

No public general-election polls are available, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the financial gap, and market pricing. A modestly favorable Democratic national environment trims the expected Republican margin slightly, but not enough to put the seat in play. Comer remains a Safe R.
